docs.title: eptr2
docs.text: eptr2 is a Python client for EPIAS Transparency Platform v2.0 - the official Turkish electricity market data platform.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• 🔌 234 API Endpoints - Access comprehensive Turkish electricity market data
  • 📊 Pandas Integration - Returns data as DataFrames for easy analysis
  • 🤖 AI Agent Ready - Built-in MCP server for Claude and other AI assistants
  • 🔑 Easy Authentication - Simple credential management with .env files
  • ♻️ TGT Recycling - Automatic ticket management for efficient API calls
  • 📈 Composite Functions - Pre-built functions for common data analysis tasks

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
from eptr2 import EPTR2

# Initialize with credentials

# Get Market Clearing Price (MCP/PTF)

print(df)

docs.title: Agent Plugin
docs.text:
eptr2 ships as a portable Agent Plugin — the vendor-neutral packaging standard for agent capabilities. The plugin bundles the two component types of the v1 specification:

  • Skills — the 7 eptr2 agent skills (SKILL.md format)
  • MCP server — the eptr2-mcp-server stdio server with 18 tools

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
The plugin root is the packaged eptr2/assets/ directory:

eptr2/assets/            <- plugin root
├── plugin.json          <- Agent Plugins manifest
├── mcp.json             <- MCP server configuration (stdio)
└── skills/
    ├── eptr2-api-discovery/
    ├── eptr2-consumption-data/
    ├── eptr2-convenience-wrappers/
    ├── eptr2-generation-tracking/
    ├── eptr2-imbalance-costs/
    ├── eptr2-market-operations/
    └── eptr2-price-analysis/

docs.title: Using the Plugin
docs.text:
Any Agent Plugins-compatible client can consume the plugin directly from the installed package:

pip install "eptr2[allextras]"
eptr2 plugin-path        # prints the plugin root inside site-packages

Point your client at that path, or copy the plugin to wherever your client discovers plugins:

eptr2 install-plugin --dest ~/.your-agent/plugins/eptr2

--force overwrites an existing copy (useful after upgrading eptr2).

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: The plugin's mcp.json intentionally contains no credentials. The MCP server reads EPTR_USERNAME / EPTR_PASSWORD from the environment or a .env file in its working directory. Configure them in your client's environment, or see MCP Client Setup for per-client examples.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: The plugin is validated in CI: the manifest is checked against the Agent Plugins 1.0.0 constraints (allowed fields, name pattern), mcp.json against the stdio transport rules, and every skill directory for a conforming SKILL.md.

docs.title: Agent Skills
docs.text: eptr2 bundles agent skills that provide specialized guidance for different types of electricity market data queries.

docs.title: What are Agent Skills?
docs.text: Agent Skills are structured knowledge files in the provider-agnostic Agent Skills format — a directory containing a SKILL.md file with trigger descriptions plus optional reference files and scripts. Compatible runtimes can consume them; discovery and automatic activation depend on the runtime configuration. The skills use standard Markdown and Python/CLI examples without vendor-specific tool allowlists.

docs.title: Installing Skills
docs.text:
The skills ship inside the pip package — no repository clone needed:

pip install eptr2
eptr2 install-skills                 # into ./.agents/skills (project)
eptr2 install-skills --dest user     # into ~/.agents/skills
eptr2 install-skills --client claude  # into ./.claude/skills
eptr2 install-skills --client claude --dest user  # into ~/.claude/skills
eptr2 install-skills --dest PATH     # anywhere your agent runtime looks for skills
eptr2 install-skills --list          # see what's bundled

The default changed from .claude/skills to .agents/skills. Existing installations are not moved, deleted, or overwritten. Use --client claude to retain the old project/user locations, or --dest PATH for any other runtime. Explicit paths take precedence over --client; leading ~ is expanded. Avoid installing duplicate copies into multiple directories scanned by the same runtime.

--only NAME selects a skill; existing directories are skipped unless --force is supplied. The same choices are available in Python:

from eptr2.agentic.skills import install_skills

install_skills()  # project .agents/skills
install_skills("user", client="claude")  # user .claude/skills

docs.text:

├── eptr2-api-discovery/         # SKILL.md + endpoint reference + script
├── eptr2-consumption-data/

├── eptr2-imbalance-costs/       # SKILL.md + examples + formulas

docs.title: Creating Custom Skills
docs.text:
You can create custom skills for your specific use cases:

  1. Create a directory in your runtime's skills location (e.g. .agents/skills/)
  2. Add a SKILL.md file with:
  3. Skill description
  4. Trigger keywords
  5. Domain knowledge
  6. Example patterns

Example structure:

# My Custom Skill

## Description
This skill helps with [specific use case].

## Triggers
- keyword1
- keyword2

## Knowledge
[Domain-specific information]

## Examples
- "Example query 1" → [Expected behavior]
- "Example query 2" → [Expected behavior]

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Be specific - Detailed queries trigger more accurate skill matching
  2. Use Turkish terms - Skills recognize both English and Turkish terminology
  3. Combine skills - Complex queries may utilize multiple skills
  4. Iterate - Follow up with clarifying questions for best results

docs.title: CLI for Agents
docs.text: The eptr2 command-line interface makes the library usable by shell-driven AI agents and humans alike. Data goes to stdout only, diagnostics to stderr, and exit codes are nonzero on error — so output can be piped and parsed safely.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Success; data (if any) is on stdout 1 The request was well-formed but failed — unknown call key, no results, authentication failure, or an API error 2 The request was malformed and never sent — invalid parameters, a bad key=value pair, or no subcommand

Code 2 means nothing reached the network, so an agent can retry only after correcting the request; code 1 may be transient.

Installed with the package:

pip install eptr2          # CLI included; pandas optional but recommended

docs.title: Discovery (no credentials needed)
docs.text:
eptr2 list                          # all 234 call keys, grouped by category
eptr2 list --category GÖP           # one category
eptr2 list --format json            # machine-readable
eptr2 categories                    # categories with endpoint counts
eptr2 search imbalance              # keyword search (English and Turkish)
eptr2 describe mcp                  # parameters, method, path, description
eptr2 describe ptf --format json    # aliases resolve automatically

docs.title: Fetching Data
docs.text:
Requires EPIAS credentials — either a .env file with EPTR_USERNAME/EPTR_PASSWORD in the working directory, or the same variables in the environment.

eptr2 call mcp --start-date 2024-07-29 --end-date 2024-07-29
eptr2 call mcp --start-date 2024-07-01 --end-date 2024-07-31 --format csv --output july.csv
eptr2 call rt-gen --start-date 2024-07-29 --end-date 2024-07-29 --format csv
eptr2 call some-key -p org_id=123 -p pp_id=456     # extra parameters

Output is JSON records by default; --format csv produces CSV.

eptr2 schema --check                # verify the committed schema is fresh (CI-friendly)

The schema covers all endpoints with parameters, plus composite functions and cost utilities. See AGENTS.md for how agents can use it.

docs.title: MCP Client Setup
docs.text: The eptr2 MCP server works with any Model Context Protocol client. This page shows the canonical configuration and per-client variants.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. eptr2 installed with MCP support: 
    pip install "eptr2[allextras]"
  2. EPIAS Transparency Platform credentials (register here)

docs.title: Canonical Configuration
docs.text:
The server is a stdio MCP server started with the eptr2-mcp-server command. Credentials are passed as environment variables:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "eptr2": {
      "command": "eptr2-mcp-server",
      "env": {
        "EPTR_USERNAME": "your.email@example.com",
        "EPTR_PASSWORD": "yourpassword"
      }
    }
  }
}

Use literal values

Most MCP clients do not expand ${VAR} placeholders in config files. Enter your credentials as literal values, or omit the env block and keep them in a .env file in the server's working directory.

You can print a ready-to-paste snippet for your client at any time:

eptr2 mcp-config --client vscode        # or: claude-desktop, claude-code, cursor, generic

docs.title: VS Code (agent mode)
docs.text:
Add the server to .vscode/mcp.json in your workspace (or via the MCP: Add Server command). Note VS Code uses a servers key:

{
  "servers": {
    "eptr2": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "eptr2-mcp-server",
      "env": {
        "EPTR_USERNAME": "your.email@example.com",
        "EPTR_PASSWORD": "yourpassword"
      }
    }
  }
}

VS Code also reads the repository's AGENTS.md natively, so agents get eptr2 usage guidance even without MCP.

docs.title: Cursor

docs.title: Any other stdio client
docs.text: Point your client at the eptr2-mcp-server command with the two environment variables. If your Python environment is not on the client's PATH, use the full path to the executable (find it with which eptr2-mcp-server) or launch via python -m eptr2.mcp.server.

docs.title: Verifying
docs.text:
Ask your assistant something like:

"What was the Turkish electricity market clearing price yesterday?"

It should call the get_market_clearing_price tool. Discovery tools (search_eptr2_calls, describe_eptr2_call) work even without credentials.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Server not found: the eptr2-mcp-server command must be on the PATH the client uses. Use an absolute path if needed.
  • Authentication errors: check the credential values; test them with eptr2 call mcp --start-date 2024-01-01 --end-date 2024-01-01 in a shell with the same environment.
  • fastmcp missing: install with pip install "eptr2[allextras]" (or eptr2[mcp]).

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text: eptr2 includes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI assistants like Claude to directly query Turkish electricity market data.

docs.title: What is MCP?
docs.text:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for connecting AI assistants to external data sources and tools. With eptr2's MCP server, AI assistants can:

  • Query real-time electricity prices
  • Fetch consumption and generation data
  • Access all 234 API endpoints
  • Perform complex market analysis

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install eptr2 with MCP support:

pip install "eptr2[allextras]"

docs.title: Running the Server
docs.text:
From command line:

eptr2-mcp-server

Or programmatically:

from eptr2.mcp import create_mcp_server, run_mcp_server
import asyncio

# Option A: async helper
asyncio.run(run_mcp_server(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True))

# Option B: explicit server creation
server = create_mcp_server(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)
# server.run()

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Create a .env file with your credentials:

EPTR_USERNAME=your.email@example.com
EPTR_PASSWORD=yourpassword

docs.text:
from eptr2.mcp import run_mcp_server
import asyncio

asyncio.run(run_mcp_server(
    use_dotenv=True,       # Load credentials from .env
    recycle_tgt=True,      # Reuse authentication tickets
    dotenv_path=".env",    # Path to .env file
))

docs.title: 2. Custom Integration
docs.text:
Use the MCP client library:

import asyncio
from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

async def main():
    server_params = StdioServerParameters(
        command="eptr2-mcp-server"
    )

    async with stdio_client(server_params) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()

            # List available tools
            tools = await session.list_tools()
            print(tools)

            # Call a tool
            result = await session.call_tool(
                "get_market_clearing_price",
                {"start_date": "2024-07-29", "end_date": "2024-07-29"}
            )
            print(result)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: eptr2.calls
docs.text:
Typed convenience wrappers for every endpoint exposed by EPTR2.call.

Each function follows the shape:

get_<endpoint>(
    <required_param>: <type>,
    ...,
    <optional_param>: <type> | None = None,
    ...,
    eptr: EPTR2 | None = None,
    **kwargs,
)

If eptr is omitted the wrapper instantiates EPTR2() on demand. Extra keyword arguments are forwarded to EPTR2.call. See the Convenience Wrappers guide for usage patterns.

docs.title: Package contents
docs.text:
import eptr2.calls as calls
print(len(calls.__all__))   # 236 (234 endpoints + 2 aliases)

The wrappers are auto-generated from src/eptr2/mapping/path.py, src/eptr2/mapping/parameters.py, and src/eptr2/mapping/help.py by scripts/generate_call_wrappers.py. Re-run the generator after adding or modifying endpoints:

python scripts/generate_call_wrappers.py

Composite functions simplify data retrieval by:

  • Combining multiple related API calls
  • Merging and transforming data
  • Handling missing data gracefully
  • Providing consistent output formats

get_hourly_consumption_and_forecast_data(start_date: str, end_date: str, eptr: EPTR2 | None = None, verbose: bool = False, include_contract_symbol: bool = True, **kwargs)

This composite function gets load plan, UECM (settlement consumption), real time and consumption data. If end date is after the last settlement data, UECM is filled with real time consumption under consumption column.

Source code in src/eptr2/composite/consumption.py 
def get_hourly_consumption_and_forecast_data(
    start_date: str,
    end_date: str,
    eptr: EPTR2 | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
    include_contract_symbol: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
):
    """
    This composite function gets load plan, UECM (settlement consumption), real time and consumption data. If end date is after the last settlement data, UECM is filled with real time consumption under consumption column.
    """

    if eptr is None:
        eptr = EPTR2(dotenv_path=kwargs.get("dotenv_path", ".env"))

    ## Transient handshake/read timeouts are exactly what retries exist for;
    ## without them a single slow response fails the whole composite.
    retry_kwargs = {
        "retry_attempts": kwargs.get("max_lives", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_RETRIES),
        "retry_backoff": kwargs.get("retry_backoff", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF),
        "retry_backoff_max": kwargs.get("retry_backoff_max", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF),
        "retry_jitter": 0.0,
    }


    if verbose:
        logger.info("Loading load plan...")

    lp_df = eptr.call(
        "load-plan",
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,
        request_kwargs={"timeout": DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_TIMEOUT},
        **retry_kwargs,
    )

    df = lp_df[["date", "lep"]].rename(columns={"lep": "load_plan", "date": "dt"})

    if verbose:
        logger.info("Loading UECM...")

    uecm_df: pd.DataFrame = eptr.call(
        "uecm", start_date=start_date, end_date=end_date, request_kwargs={"timeout": DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_TIMEOUT}, **retry_kwargs
    )

    if not uecm_df.empty:
        uecm_df = uecm_df[["period", "swv"]].rename(
            columns={"period": "dt", "swv": "uecm"}
        )

        df = df.merge(
            uecm_df,
            on="dt",
            how="outer",
        )

    if verbose:
        logger.info("Loading real time consumption...")

    rt_cons = eptr.call(
        "rt-cons",
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,
        request_kwargs={"timeout": DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_TIMEOUT},
        **retry_kwargs,
    )

    df = df.merge(
        rt_cons[["date", "consumption"]].rename(
            columns={"date": "dt", "consumption": "rt_cons"}
        ),
        on="dt",
        how="outer",
    )

    if not uecm_df.empty:
        df["consumption"] = df.apply(
            lambda x: x["rt_cons"] if pd.isnull(x["uecm"]) else x["uecm"], axis=1
        )
    else:
        df["consumption"] = df["rt_cons"].copy()

    if include_contract_symbol:
        try:
            df["contract"] = df["dt"].apply(lambda x: iso_to_contract(x))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Contract information could not be added. Error: %s", e)

    return df

This composite function gets price and imbalance (kupst included) cost data. Imbalance cost data consists of MCP (PTF), SMP (SMF), system direction (Enerji Açığı - up regulated, Energy Fazlası - down regulated, Dengede - Balanced), positive imbalance cost and negative imbalance cost.

Resulting columns are: - date: Datetime in ISO format and +03:00 timezone - mcp: Market Clearing Price (MCP/PTF) in TL (Turkish Lira) - smp: System Marginal Price (SMP/SMF) in TL (Turkish Lira) - wap: Weighted Average Price (WAP) in TL (Turkish Lira) - system_direction: System direction (Enerji Açığı - up regulated, Energy Fazlası - down regulated, Dengede - Balanced) - sd_sign: System direction sign (1 for Enerji Fazlası, -1 for Enerji Açığı, 0 for Dengede) - pos_imb_price: Positive imbalance price in TL (Turkish Lira) - neg_imb_price: Negative imbalance price in TL (Turkish Lira) (negative value) - pos_imb_cost: Positive imbalance cost in TL (Turkish Lira) (ptf - pos_imb_price) - neg_imb_cost: Negative imbalance cost in TL (Turkish Lira) (neg_imb_price - ptf)

def get_hourly_price_and_cost_data(
    start_date: str,
    end_date: str,
    eptr: EPTR2 | None = None,
    include_wap: bool = True,
    add_kupst_cost: bool = True,
    verbose: bool = False,
    include_contract_symbol: bool = True,
    timeout: int = 10,
    add_unit_prefix_to_cost_colnames: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
):
    """
    This composite function gets price and imbalance (kupst included) cost data.
    Imbalance cost data consists of MCP (PTF), SMP (SMF), system direction (Enerji Açığı - up regulated, Energy Fazlası - down regulated, Dengede - Balanced), positive imbalance cost and negative imbalance cost.

    Resulting columns are:
    - date: Datetime in ISO format and +03:00 timezone
    - mcp: Market Clearing Price (MCP/PTF) in TL (Turkish Lira)
    - smp: System Marginal Price (SMP/SMF) in TL (Turkish Lira)
    - wap: Weighted Average Price (WAP) in TL (Turkish Lira)
    - system_direction: System direction (Enerji Açığı - up regulated, Energy Fazlası - down regulated, Dengede - Balanced)
    - sd_sign: System direction sign (1 for Enerji Fazlası, -1 for Enerji Açığı, 0 for Dengede)
    - pos_imb_price: Positive imbalance price in TL (Turkish Lira)
    - neg_imb_price: Negative imbalance price in TL (Turkish Lira) (negative value)
    - pos_imb_cost: Positive imbalance cost in TL (Turkish Lira) (ptf - pos_imb_price)
    - neg_imb_cost: Negative imbalance cost in TL (Turkish Lira) (neg_imb_price - ptf)
    """

    if eptr is None:
        eptr = EPTR2(dotenv_path=kwargs.get("dotenv_path", ".env"))

    retry_kwargs = {
        "retry_attempts": kwargs.get("max_lives", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_RETRIES),
        "retry_backoff": kwargs.get("retry_backoff", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF),
        "retry_backoff_max": kwargs.get("retry_backoff_max", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF),
        "retry_jitter": 0.0,
    }

    if verbose:
        logger.info("Getting MCP, SMP and imbalance price data...")

    price_df = eptr.call(
        "mcp-smp-imb",
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,
        request_kwargs={"timeout": timeout},
        **retry_kwargs,
    )

    price_df.drop(columns=["time"], inplace=True)

    price_df.rename(
        columns={
            "ptf": "mcp",
            "smf": "smp",
            "positiveImbalance": "pos_imb_price",
            "negativeImbalance": "neg_imb_price",
            "systemStatus": "system_direction",
        },
        inplace=True,
    )

    price_df["sd_sign"] = price_df["system_direction"].apply(
        lambda x: -1 if x == "Enerji Açığı" else 1 if x == "Enerji Fazlası" else 0
    )

    price_df["pos_imb_cost"] = price_df["mcp"] - price_df["pos_imb_price"]
    price_df["neg_imb_cost"] = price_df["neg_imb_price"] - price_df["mcp"]

    if include_wap:
        if verbose:
            logger.info("Getting WAP data...")

        wap_df = eptr.call(
            "wap",
            start_date=start_date,
            end_date=end_date,
            request_kwargs={"timeout": timeout},
            **retry_kwargs,
        )
        wap_df.drop(columns=["hour"], inplace=True)

        price_df = price_df.merge(wap_df, on="date", how="outer")

    if include_contract_symbol or add_kupst_cost:
        try:
            price_df["contract"] = price_df["date"].apply(lambda x: iso_to_contract(x))
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Contract information could not be added. Error: %s", e)

    if add_kupst_cost:
        if verbose:
            logger.info("Calculating unit KUPST cost...")

        added_params = {
            k: v
            for k, v in kwargs.items()
            if k
            in [
                "kupst_multiplier",
                "kupst_floor_price",
                "include_maintenance_penalty",
            ]
        }
        ## KUPST multipliers depend on the KUPST category (e.g. 'wind',
        ## 'plant_w_battery') from 2026-11-01. Default is 'other'.
        if kwargs.get("kupst_category") is not None:
            added_params["category"] = kwargs["kupst_category"]

        price_df["kupst_cost"] = price_df.apply(
            lambda x: calculate_unit_kupst_cost_by_contract(
                contract=x["contract"],
                mcp=x["mcp"],
                smp=x["smp"],
                **added_params,
            ),
            axis=1,
        )

        if not include_contract_symbol:
            price_df.drop(columns=["contract"], inplace=True)

    ### Column ordering
    columns_order = [
        "date",
        "contract",
        "pos_imb_vol",
        "neg_imb_vol",
        "pos_imb_mwh",
        "neg_imb_mwh",
        "mcp",
        "wap",
        "smp",
        "pos_imb_price",
        "neg_imb_price",
        "system_direction",
        "sd_sign",
        "pos_imb_cost",
        "neg_imb_cost",
        "kupst_cost",
    ]

    if add_unit_prefix_to_cost_colnames:
        cost_cols_mapping = {
            "pos_imb_cost": "unit_pos_imb_cost",
            "neg_imb_cost": "unit_neg_imb_cost",
            "kupst_cost": "unit_kupst_cost",
        }
        price_df.rename(columns=cost_cols_mapping, inplace=True)
        for old_col, new_col in cost_cols_mapping.items():
            if old_col in columns_order:
                columns_order.remove(old_col)
                columns_order.append(new_col)

    columns_order = [col for col in columns_order if col in price_df.columns]

    price_df = price_df[columns_order]

    return price_df

This composite function gets production data (Gerçek Zamanlı Üretim, UEVM) and merges them.

It is also possible to enter pp_id to get the production data for a specific production plan. Example ID values are given below.

rt_pp_id=641, ## ATATÜRK HES uevm_pp_id=142, ## ATATÜRK HES

def get_hourly_production_data(
    start_date: str,
    end_date: str,
    eptr: EPTR2 | None = None,
    rt_pp_id: str | int | None = None,
    uevm_pp_id: str | int | None = None,
    verbose: bool = False,
    include_contract_symbol: bool = True,
    skip_uevm: bool = False,
    skip_rt: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
):
    """
    This composite function gets production data (Gerçek Zamanlı Üretim, UEVM) and merges them.

    It is also possible to enter pp_id to get the production data for a specific production plan. Example ID values are given below.

    rt_pp_id=641, ## ATATÜRK HES
    uevm_pp_id=142, ## ATATÜRK HES
    """

    if eptr is None:
        eptr = EPTR2(dotenv_path=kwargs.get("dotenv_path", ".env"))

    max_trials = kwargs.get("max_trials", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_RETRIES)
    timeout = kwargs.get("timeout", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_TIMEOUT)
    sleep_interval = kwargs.get("sleep_interval", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF)
    retry_kwargs = {
        "retry_attempts": max_trials,
        "retry_backoff": sleep_interval,
        "retry_backoff_max": sleep_interval,
        "retry_jitter": 0.0,
    }

    ## A missing plant id means "no plant filter", not "skip this source":
    ## rt-gen and uevm both return system-wide totals without one. Only skip
    ## the other source when exactly one plant is requested, so plant-level and
    ## system-wide figures are never merged into the same frame. Explicit
    ## skip_rt / skip_uevm always win.
    if rt_pp_id is None and uevm_pp_id is not None:
        skip_rt = True
    if uevm_pp_id is None and rt_pp_id is not None:
        skip_uevm = True

    #### SANITY CHECKS ####
    if skip_rt and skip_uevm:
        raise ValueError("Both skip_rt and skip_uevm cannot be True.")

    #### REAL TIME GENERATION PHASE ####
    if skip_rt:
        rt_included = False
        rt_gen_df = pd.DataFrame()

    else:
        rt_included = True
        if verbose:
            logger.info("Loading real time production data...")

        rt_gen_df: pd.DataFrame = eptr.call(
            "rt-gen",
            start_date=start_date,
            end_date=end_date,
            pp_id=rt_pp_id,
            request_kwargs={"timeout": timeout},
            **retry_kwargs,
        )

        if rt_gen_df.empty:
            raise ValueError("No data (production) is available for this date range.")

        try:
            rt_gen_df.drop("hour", axis=1, inplace=True)
        except Exception as e:
            if verbose:
                logger.info("%s", e)

        rt_gen_df.columns = [
            x + "_rt" if x not in ["date"] else x for x in rt_gen_df.columns
        ]

    #### UEVM PHASE ####
    if skip_uevm:
        uevm_included = False
        uevm_df = pd.DataFrame()

    else:
        uevm_included = True
        if verbose:
            logger.info("Loading UEVM data...")

        uevm_df: pd.DataFrame = eptr.call(
            "uevm",
            start_date=start_date,
            end_date=end_date,
            pp_id=uevm_pp_id,
            request_kwargs={"timeout": timeout},
            **retry_kwargs,
        )

        try:
            uevm_df.drop("hour", axis=1, inplace=True)
        except Exception as e:
            within_settlement = check_date_for_settlement(x=end_date)
            if not within_settlement:
                logger.warning("The end date may not be within the settlement period.")
            if verbose:
                logger.info("%s", e)

        uevm_df.columns = [
            x + "_uevm" if x not in ["date"] else x for x in uevm_df.columns
        ]

    if uevm_included and rt_included:
        if verbose:
            logger.info("Merging data...")

        if uevm_df.empty:
            merged_df = rt_gen_df.copy()
        else:
            merged_df = rt_gen_df.merge(uevm_df, how="left", on=["date"])
    elif uevm_included:
        merged_df = uevm_df.copy()
    elif rt_included:
        merged_df = rt_gen_df.copy()

    if include_contract_symbol:
        try:
            merged_df["contract"] = merged_df["date"].apply(
                lambda x: iso_to_contract(x)
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Contract information could not be added. Error: %s", e)

    merged_df = merged_df.rename(columns={"date": "dt"})

    return merged_df

get_org_estimated_activity(start_date: str, end_date: str, org_id: str | int, eptr: EPTR2 | None = None, include_pnl: bool = False, include_tad: bool = False, idm_log_df: DataFrame | None = None, export_to_csv: bool = False, export_dir: str = 'data', check_existing: bool = True, verbose: bool = True, **kwargs) -> DataFrame

Estimates an organization's (company's) trading activity for the given period (start_date and end_date inclusive) on an hourly contract basis.

The activity comes from the organization's own matched quantities only: day ahead (GÖP), bilateral (İA) and intraday (GİP) matchings by organization id (get_dabi_idm_data, a few seconds per week). See calculate_org_activity for the decomposition (day ahead open / intraday close, day trade, dabi_net and dabi_idm_net net positions).

With include_pnl=True a fictitious PnL of day ahead open / intraday close trades is added from MCP and the published intraday WAP (two more calls, fast).

With include_tad=True the TAD (total absolute deviation) of each contract (idm_tad) and day_trade_tad = day_trade * TAD are added. These are volatility metrics, not PnL. TAD can only be calculated from the market wide intraday trade log (idm_log_longer), which is large (about 20k trades a day), so this is much slower. The log is fetched in multi-day chunks by idm_log_longer; pass idm_log_days_interval to change the chunk length (days_interval of idm_log_longer).

With export_to_csv=True the raw data and the result are written to export_dir as CSV files named {name}{start_date}}.csv: org_{org_idpositions (get_dabi_idm_data output), mcp and wap (raw mcp and wap calls), idm_log (the market wide trade log), idm_contract_stats (per contract WAP, TAD, trade count and volume from the log) and org_activity (the returned frame). Only the data of the requested steps is written. With check_existing=True, files of the same name (same period) are read from export_dir instead of being fetched, so the market wide files (mcp, wap, idm_log) are recycled for other organizations of the same period. CSV is used because the trade log can exceed the Excel row limit.

end_date must be before today (Europe/Istanbul): data of the current day is not final, so neither the result nor the exported files would be.

def get_org_estimated_activity(
    start_date: str,
    end_date: str,
    org_id: str | int,
    eptr: EPTR2 | None = None,
    include_pnl: bool = False,
    include_tad: bool = False,
    idm_log_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None,
    export_to_csv: bool = False,
    export_dir: str = "data",
    check_existing: bool = True,
    verbose: bool = True,
    **kwargs,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Estimates an organization's (company's) trading activity for the given period (start_date and end_date inclusive) on an hourly contract basis.

    The activity comes from the organization's own matched quantities only: day ahead (GÖP), bilateral (İA) and intraday (GİP) matchings by organization id (get_dabi_idm_data, a few seconds per week). See calculate_org_activity for the decomposition (day ahead open / intraday close, day trade, dabi_net and dabi_idm_net net positions).

    With include_pnl=True a fictitious PnL of day ahead open / intraday close trades is added from MCP and the published intraday WAP (two more calls, fast).

    With include_tad=True the TAD (total absolute deviation) of each contract (idm_tad) and day_trade_tad = day_trade * TAD are added. These are volatility metrics, not PnL. TAD can only be calculated from the market wide intraday trade log (idm_log_longer), which is large (about 20k trades a day), so this is much slower. The log is fetched in multi-day chunks by idm_log_longer; pass idm_log_days_interval to change the chunk length (days_interval of idm_log_longer).

    With export_to_csv=True the raw data and the result are written to export_dir as CSV files named {name}_{start_date}_{end_date}.csv: org_{org_id}_positions (get_dabi_idm_data output), mcp and wap (raw mcp and wap calls), idm_log (the market wide trade log), idm_contract_stats (per contract WAP, TAD, trade count and volume from the log) and org_{org_id}_activity (the returned frame). Only the data of the requested steps is written. With check_existing=True, files of the same name (same period) are read from export_dir instead of being fetched, so the market wide files (mcp, wap, idm_log) are recycled for other organizations of the same period. CSV is used because the trade log can exceed the Excel row limit.

    end_date must be before today (Europe/Istanbul): data of the current day is not final, so neither the result nor the exported files would be.

    Args:
        start_date: Start date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format
        end_date: End date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format (inclusive), before today
        org_id: Organization ID
        eptr: EPTR2 object. Created from .env if not provided.
        include_pnl: Add mcp, idm_wap and dabi_idm_pnl (fetches MCP and WAP).
        include_tad: Add idm_tad and day_trade_tad (fetches the IDM trade log). Independent of include_pnl.
        idm_log_df: Previously fetched IDM trade log covering the period (e.g. idm_log_longer output). The log is market wide, so it can be reused for several organizations to avoid fetching it again. Implies include_tad=True.
        export_to_csv: Write the raw data and the result to export_dir as CSV files (see above).
        export_dir: Directory of the CSV files, created if missing.
        check_existing: Read the raw data from existing CSV files of the same period in export_dir instead of fetching it.
        verbose: Log each step and each IDM log chunk with row counts and elapsed time (to stderr)

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: One row per hourly contract with quantity and decomposition columns, and the price, PnL and TAD columns that were requested. Prices (mcp, idm_wap, idm_tad) are left NaN if they could not be retrieved, they are not filled with 0.
    """
    today = get_today_utc3()
    if end_date >= today:
        raise ValueError(
            f"end_date must be before today ({today}, Europe/Istanbul): data of the current day is not final. Got end_date={end_date}."
        )

    t_start = time.time()

    def log_step(message, *args):
        if verbose:
            logger.info("[%5.1fs] " + message, time.time() - t_start, *args)

    if export_to_csv:
        os.makedirs(export_dir, exist_ok=True)

    ## Files read with check_existing are not written again
    loaded = set()

    def csv_path(name):
        return os.path.join(export_dir, f"{name}_{start_date}_{end_date}.csv")

    def load_existing(name):
        path = csv_path(name)
        if not (check_existing and os.path.exists(path)):
            return None
        log_step("Reading %s from %s", name, path)
        loaded.add(name)
        return pd.read_csv(path, dtype={"contract": str, "contractName": str})

    def export(df, name):
        if export_to_csv and name not in loaded:
            df.to_csv(csv_path(name), index=False)
            log_step("Wrote %d rows to %s", len(df), csv_path(name))

    if idm_log_df is not None:
        include_tad = True

    if eptr is None:
        eptr = EPTR2(dotenv_path=kwargs.get("dotenv_path", ".env"))

    retry_kwargs = {
        "retry_attempts": kwargs.get("lives", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_RETRIES),
        "retry_backoff": kwargs.get("retry_backoff", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF),
        "retry_backoff_max": kwargs.get(
            "retry_backoff_max", kwargs.get("retry_backoff", DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_BACKOFF)
        ),
        "retry_jitter": kwargs.get("retry_jitter", 0.0),
    }

    log_step(
        "Getting GÖP, İA and GİP matchings of organization %s for %s to %s...",
        org_id,
        start_date,
        end_date,
    )
    pos_name = f"org_{org_id}_positions"
    pos_df = load_existing(pos_name)
    if pos_df is None:
        pos_df = get_dabi_idm_data(
            start_date=start_date,
            end_date=end_date,
            eptr=eptr,
            org_id=org_id,
            verbose=verbose,
            **kwargs,
        )
    log_step("Got matchings for %d hour(s).", len(pos_df))
    export(pos_df, pos_name)

    ## All hourly contracts of the period, so that missing rows of any source do not drop contracts
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "contract": get_hourly_contract_range_list(
                start_date=start_date, end_date=end_date
            )
        }
    )
    pos_cols = ["contract", "date"] + [
        c for c in QUANTITY_COLUMNS if c in pos_df.columns
    ]
    df = df.merge(pos_df[pos_cols], on="contract", how="left")
    for col in QUANTITY_COLUMNS:
        if col not in df.columns:
            df[col] = 0.0
        df[col] = df[col].fillna(0.0)

    if include_pnl:
        mcp_df = load_existing("mcp")
        if mcp_df is None:
            log_step("Getting MCP...")
            mcp_df = eptr.call(
                "mcp",
                start_date=start_date,
                end_date=end_date,
                request_kwargs={"timeout": DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_TIMEOUT},
                **retry_kwargs,
            )
        export(mcp_df, "mcp")
        mcp_df = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "contract": mcp_df["date"].apply(lambda x: iso_to_contract(x)),
                "mcp": mcp_df["price"],
            }
        )

        wap_df = load_existing("wap")
        if wap_df is None:
            log_step("Getting intraday WAP...")
            wap_df = eptr.call(
                "wap",
                start_date=start_date,
                end_date=end_date,
                request_kwargs={"timeout": DEFAULT_COMPOSITE_TIMEOUT},
                **retry_kwargs,
            )
        export(wap_df, "wap")
        wap_df = pd.DataFrame(
            {
                "contract": wap_df["date"].apply(lambda x: iso_to_contract(x)),
                "idm_wap": wap_df["wap"],
            }
        )

        ## Missing prices stay NaN so that PnL is not silently zeroed
        df = df.merge(mcp_df, on="contract", how="left").merge(
            wap_df, on="contract", how="left"
        )

        if df["idm_wap"].isna().any():
            logger.warning(
                "IDM WAP is missing for %d contract(s), their intraday PnL is NaN.",
                int(df["idm_wap"].isna().sum()),
            )

    if include_tad:
        if idm_log_df is None:
            idm_log_df = load_existing("idm_log")
        if idm_log_df is None:
            log_step(
                "Getting the IDM trade log for TAD (market wide, about 20k trades a day)..."
            )
            ## idm_log_longer fetches wide ranges in chunks of days_interval (+1) days
            log_kwargs = (
                {"days_interval": kwargs["idm_log_days_interval"]}
                if "idm_log_days_interval" in kwargs
                else {}
            )
            idm_log_df = idm_log_longer(
                start_date=start_date,
                end_date=end_date,
                eptr=eptr,
                contract_wise=True,
                verbose=verbose,
                **log_kwargs,
            )
            log_step("Got %d IDM trades.", len(idm_log_df))
        export(idm_log_df, "idm_log")
        stats_df = calculate_idm_contract_stats(idm_log_df)
        export(stats_df, "idm_contract_stats")
        df = df.merge(stats_df[["contract", "idm_tad"]], on="contract", how="left")

    df = calculate_org_activity(df)
    df["org_id"] = org_id
    export(df, f"org_{org_id}_activity")
    log_step("Done.")

    return df

docs.text:
calculate_org_activity(df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame

Decomposes an organization's hourly positions into day ahead / intraday trades, day trades and net positions and, if prices are given, adds a fictitious (estimated) PnL.

Required columns: da_long, da_short, idm_long, idm_short. Optional columns: bi_long, bi_short (taken as 0 if missing); mcp and idm_wap (add dabi_idm_pnl); idm_tad (adds day_trade_tad).

Added columns (all quantities in MWh, positive is buy / long): da_net: da_long - da_short bi_net: bi_long - bi_short dabi_net: da_net + bi_net. Day ahead (GÖP + İA) net position. idm_net: idm_long - idm_short dabi_idm_net: dabi_net + idm_net. Net quantity that shall either be consumed (positive, net buyer) or generated (negative, net seller). Subtract bi_net for the organized market (GÖP + GİP) only part. day_trade: min(idm_long, idm_short). Intraday quantity bought and sold back within the intraday market. dabi_idm_close: Day ahead (GÖP + İA) position closed (reversed) in the intraday market. min(|dabi_net|, |idm_net|) if dabi_net and idm_net have opposite signs, otherwise 0. Always non-negative, direction follows dabi_net. dabi_idm_pnl: Fictitious PnL of day ahead open / intraday close trades. dabi_idm_close * sign(dabi_net) * (idm_wap - mcp). Buying day ahead and selling in IDM gains when idm_wap > mcp, the reverse for selling day ahead. Bilateral quantities are valued at mcp as well. day_trade_tad: Only with idm_tad. day_trade * idm_tad (TL). A volatility metric of the day trade volume, the price room around WAP it was traded in; it is not a PnL. Note that this is one sided TAD (not 2 * TAD for a buy and a sell around WAP) by definition.

The PnL is an estimate: actual trade prices of the organization are not public, so intraday trades are assumed to be at idm_wap. If a price is missing, the related PnL is NaN.

def call(self, key: str, **kwargs):
    """
    Main call function for the API. This function is used to process parameters and make calls to EPIAS Transparency API.
    """

    self.check_renew_tgt(**kwargs)
    raw_key = key
    key = alias_to_path(alias=key, custom_aliases=self.custom_aliases)

    if key not in self.path_map_keys:
        if raw_key == key:
            raise Exception(
                f"This call {raw_key} is not yet defined in calls or aliases. Call 'get_available_calls' method to see the available calls."
            )
        else:
            raise Exception(
                f"This alias {raw_key} forwarded to key {key} is not yet defined in calls. Call 'get_available_calls' method to see the available calls."
            )

    call_path = get_total_path(key)
    call_method = get_call_method(key)
    required_body_params = get_required_parameters(key)
    call_body_raw = kwargs.pop("call_body", kwargs)

    ### There are some calls requiring special handling, they have a special function to process them
    call_body_raw = process_special_calls(key, call_body_raw)

    optional_body_params = get_optional_parameters(key)
    all_params = required_body_params + optional_body_params

    ## Unrecognized parameters used to be dropped silently, which could
    ## change the meaning of a request rather than fail it: a misspelled
    ## filter (e.g. `ppID` instead of `pp_id`) turned a filtered query into
    ## an unfiltered one that still returned a plausible-looking result.
    unknown_params = [
        k
        for k in call_body_raw
        if k not in all_params and k not in RESERVED_CALL_OPTIONS
    ]
    if unknown_params:
        ## Match case- and underscore-insensitively so the common
        ## camelCase/snake_case mix-ups (ppID -> pp_id) are suggested.
        def _norm(name):
            return name.replace("_", "").lower()

        normalized = {_norm(p): p for p in all_params}
        suggestions = {}
        for bad_key in unknown_params:
            exact = normalized.get(_norm(bad_key))
            if exact:
                suggestions[bad_key] = [exact]
                continue
            close = difflib.get_close_matches(
                _norm(bad_key), list(normalized), n=2, cutoff=0.6
            )
            if close:
                suggestions[bad_key] = [normalized[c] for c in close]
        hint = (
            " Did you mean: "
            + "; ".join(f"{k} -> {', '.join(v)}" for k, v in suggestions.items())
            + "."
            if suggestions
            else ""
        )
        detail = (
            f"Call '{key}' does not accept parameter(s) "
            f"{sorted(unknown_params)}. Accepted parameters: "
            f"{sorted(all_params)}.{hint}"
        )

        strict_params = kwargs.get(
            "strict_params", self.__dict__.get("strict_params", False)
        )
        if strict_params:
            raise ValueError(detail)

        warnings.warn(
            detail
            + " The request is sent WITHOUT them, so any filtering they were"
            + " meant to apply will not take effect. Pass strict_params=True"
            + " (per call or on EPTR2) to raise instead.",
            UserWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )

    ## Generated wrappers forward unset optional parameters as None; an
    ## optional None means "not given" (a None date would crash preprocessing)
    call_body = {
        k: preprocess_parameter(k, v)
        for k, v in call_body_raw.items()  ## If there is a call_body parameter in kwargsi, use it, else use kwargs
        if k in all_params and not (v is None and k not in required_body_params)
    }

    for body_key in required_body_params:
        if body_key not in call_body.keys():
            call_body[body_key] = preprocess_parameter(body_key, None)
        kwargs.pop(body_key, None)

    if call_body is not None:
        if not all([x in call_body.keys() for x in required_body_params]):
            raise Exception("Some required parameters are missing in call body.")

        if kwargs.get("map_param_labels", True):
            cb2 = {}
            for k, v in call_body.items():
                ## Updated this part to handle multiple labels originating from a single label
                label = get_param_label(k)["label"]
                value = v
                if isinstance(label, list):
                    for l in label:  # noqa: E741
                        cb2[l] = value
                else:
                    cb2[label] = value
            call_body = copy.deepcopy(cb2)

    elif len(required_body_params) > 0:
        raise Exception("Required parameters are missing in call body.")

    ## If the call is uevm, change powerPlantId to powerplantId due to only non-standard naming in powerPlantId
    if key == "uevm" and "powerPlantId" in call_body.keys():
        call_body["powerplantId"] = call_body.pop("powerPlantId")

    if key in ["bpm-orders-w-avg"]:
        call_body["page"] = {"number": 1, "size": 24}

    kwargs.setdefault(
        "connect_timeout",
        self.__dict__.get("connect_timeout", DEFAULT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT),
    )
    kwargs.setdefault(
        "read_timeout",
        self.__dict__.get("read_timeout", DEFAULT_READ_TIMEOUT),
    )

    res = transparency_call(
        call_path=call_path,
        call_method=call_method,
        call_body=call_body,
        root_phrase=self.root_phrase,
        ssl_verify=self.ssl_verify,
        is_test=self.is_test,
        tgt=self.tgt,
        **kwargs,
    )

    ## Set soft timeout for tgt renewal
    self.tgt_exp_0 = min(
        self.tgt_exp,
        datetime.now().timestamp() + 60 * 90,
    )

    if self.recycle_tgt:
        self.export_tgt_info()

    if kwargs.get("get_raw_response", self.get_raw_response):
        return res

    res = json.loads(res.data.decode("utf-8"))
    if kwargs.get("postprocess", self.postprocess):
        from eptr2.mapping.processing import get_postprocess_function

        df = get_postprocess_function(key)(res, key=key)
        return df

    return res

    if self.username is None or self.password is None:
        raise Exception("Username and password must be provided for tgt renewal.")

    test_suffix = "-prp" if self.is_test else ""
    login_url = f"""https://giris{test_suffix}.epias.com.tr/cas/v1/tickets"""

    body_str = f"username={quote(self.username)}&password={quote(self.password)}"

    http = urllib3.PoolManager(
        cert_reqs="CERT_REQUIRED" if self.ssl_verify else "CERT_NONE"
    )

    res = http.request(
        method="POST",
        url=login_url,
        headers={
            "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded",
            "Accept": "text/plain",
        },
        body=body_str,
        **apply_default_timeout(
            kwargs.get("request_kwargs"),
            ## Login kept its own 10s bound before default timeouts existed;
            ## preserve it rather than relaxing the read side to 60s.
            connect_timeout=self.__dict__.get(
                "connect_timeout", DEFAULT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT
            ),
            read_timeout=self.__dict__.get("read_timeout", DEFAULT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT)
            if "read_timeout" in self.__dict__
            else DEFAULT_LOGIN_TIMEOUT,
        ),
    )
    if res.status not in [200, 201]:
        raise Exception(
            "Request failed with status code: "
            + str(res.status)
            + ": "
            + res.data.decode("utf-8")
        )

    if isinstance(res.data, bytes):
        res_data = res.data.decode("utf-8")
    else:
        res_data = res.data

    if res_data.startswith("TGT-"):
        tgt = res_data
    else:
        raise Exception("Login failed. TGT not found in response: " + res_data)

    self.tgt = tgt
    tgt_start_time = datetime.now()

    ## Hard timeout
    self.tgt_exp = (tgt_start_time + timedelta(hours=1, minutes=45)).timestamp()

    ## Soft timeout
    self.tgt_exp_0 = min(
        self.tgt_exp,
        (tgt_start_time + timedelta(hours=1, minutes=45)).timestamp(),
    )

    if self.recycle_tgt:
        self.export_tgt_info()

docs.title: eptr2.util.costs
docs.text:
Imbalance and KÜPST (production plan deviation) prices and costs. Start with the two main functions: they resolve every regulation parameter (floor and ceiling prices, V, B, margins, KÜPST tolerance and multiplier by category) for each hour from its delivery date, so a range spanning regulation changes is priced hour by hour. EPİAŞ's published imbalance prices are used where available; they are calculated only for hours without them. Hours without SMP (such as the rest of the current day) are skipped with a warning.

from eptr2.util.costs import calculate_imbalance_prices, calculate_imbalance_costs

## Hourly prices, unit costs and every parameter used (fetches mcp-smp-imb)
prices_df = calculate_imbalance_prices("2026-10-01", "2026-10-07", eptr=eptr)

## Imbalance and KÜPST costs of actual vs forecast rows
costs_df = calculate_imbalance_costs(
    data=[
        {"date": "2026-11-01T10:00:00+03:00", "actual": 80, "forecast": 100},
        {"date": "2026-11-01T11:00:00+03:00", "actual": 95, "forecast": 90},
    ],
    category="Rüzgar",  # any naming convention, see normalize_kupst_category
    eptr=eptr,
)

## Offline or scenario prices: pass them instead of fetching
calculate_imbalance_prices(
    prices=[{"date": "2026-11-01T00:00:00+03:00", "mcp": 120, "smp": 130,
             "system_direction": -1}],
    kupst_category="wind",
)

The dated regulation table is get_time_regulation_params_map(); each row names its period (26_01 from 2026-01-01, 26_02 from 2026-11-01).

docs.title: calculate_imbalance_prices

calculate_imbalance_prices(start_date: str | datetime | None = None, end_date: str | datetime | None = None, prices: DataFrame | list[dict] | None = None, eptr: EPTR2 | None = None, kupst_category: str = 'other', include_maintenance_penalty: bool = False, return_df: bool = True, include_calculated: bool = False, **kwargs: float) -> DataFrame | list[dict]

Hourly imbalance prices, unit costs and every regulation parameter used to calculate them, resolved automatically from each hour's delivery date.

For each hour the regulation period, price floor and ceiling, V, B, low, high and ceiling margins and the KUPST tolerance, multiplier and floor price are looked up (see get_time_regulation_params_map and contract_to_floor_ceil_prices), so a range spanning regulation changes is priced correctly hour by hour.

Market prices come from prices if given, otherwise they are fetched from EPİAŞ (mcp-smp-imb) for the range. Where the published imbalance prices are available (always for fetched hours, or 'positiveImbalance' / 'negativeImbalance' in prices) they are used as pos_imb_price and neg_imb_price, and the unit costs follow from them. Otherwise the prices are calculated from MCP, SMP, system direction and the resolved parameters, e.g. for scenarios or offline use.

Hours without SMP and published prices cannot be priced and are skipped with a warning. EPİAŞ returns every hour of the current day, those after the latest published hour without SMP, so a range ending today returns its published hours only. If no hour has SMP, ValueError is raised. For future hours pass prices with an SMP scenario.

None end_date str | datetime | None

Hourly prices as a DataFrame or list of dicts with 'date' (or 'contract'), 'mcp' (or 'ptf') and 'smp' (or 'smf'), and optionally 'system_direction' (-1/0/1, or EPİAŞ 'systemStatus' labels such as 'Enerji Açığı'). The raw mcp-smp-imb response is accepted as is. Rows outside start_date/end_date are dropped.

KUPST category or source name for the KUPST columns (see normalize_kupst_category).

Use the KUPST maintenance multiplier.

False return_df bool

Return a pandas DataFrame if pandas is installed, otherwise (or if False) a list of dicts.

True include_calculated bool

Also return calculated_pos_imb_price and calculated_neg_imb_price, to check the resolved parameters against the published prices.

False **kwargs float

docs.title: normalize_kupst_category
docs.text:
normalize_kupst_category(name: str | None, strict: bool = False) -> str

Map a source or category name in any common naming convention to one of KUPST_CATEGORIES.

Matching ignores case, Turkish characters and separators: Turkish characters are folded to ASCII (ı/İ -> i, ş -> s, ğ -> g, ü -> u, ö -> o, ç -> c), so 'Rüzgar', 'ruzgar' and 'RUZGAR' are the same. 'RES', 'wind', 'Güneş', 'GES', 'PV', 'Depolamalı üretim tesisi', 'wind + battery', 'Müstakil depolama', 'BESS', 'İletime bağlı lisanssız', 'Dağıtıma bağlı lisanssız', 'unlicensed', 'HES', 'doğalgaz' all resolve.

Rules, in order: an exact category name or alias; unlicensed (distribution if a distribution keyword is present, transmission otherwise); battery (plant_w_battery if it is a generation plant with storage, battery if it is standalone storage); wind; solar; other sources.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str | None

Source or category name. None gives 'other'.

required strict bool

If True, raise ValueError for names that match no rule instead of returning 'other'.

False

One of KUPST_CATEGORIES.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: eptr2 requires credentials from the EPIAS Transparency Platform to access market data.

docs.title: Getting Credentials
docs.text:
1. Visit the EPIAS registration page
  2. Complete the registration form
  3. Verify your email address
  4. Use your registration email and password as credentials

docs.title: Method 1: Environment File (Recommended)
docs.text:
Create a .env file in your project directory:

.env
EPTR_USERNAME=your.email@example.com
EPTR_PASSWORD=yourpassword

Then initialize without explicit credentials:

from eptr2 import EPTR2

eptr = EPTR2(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)

TGT Recycling

Setting recycle_tgt=True stores the authentication ticket locally (.eptr2-tgt file) and reuses it until expiration. This reduces API calls and avoids rate limiting.

docs.title: Method 2: Direct Credentials
docs.text:
Pass credentials directly (useful for quick testing):

from eptr2 import EPTR2

eptr = EPTR2(
    username="your.email@example.com",
    password="yourpassword"
)

Security

Never commit credentials to version control. Use environment files or environment variables instead.

docs.title: Method 3: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set system environment variables:

Linux/macOSWindows 
export EPTR_USERNAME="your.email@example.com"
export EPTR_PASSWORD="yourpassword"

$env:EPTR_USERNAME = "your.email@example.com"
$env:EPTR_PASSWORD = "yourpassword"

Then initialize:

from eptr2 import EPTR2

eptr = EPTR2()  # Automatically reads from environment

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
The EPTR2 class accepts several authentication-related options:

Parameter Type Default Description username str None EPIAS platform username (email) password str None EPIAS platform password use_dotenv bool True Load credentials from .env file dotenv_path str ".env" Path to the .env file recycle_tgt bool True Reuse authentication tickets tgt_path str "." Directory to store TGT file force_renew_tgt bool False Force renewal of TGT

docs.title: TGT (Ticket Granting Ticket) Management
docs.text:
eptr2 uses a ticket-based authentication system:

  1. Initial Login: Credentials are exchanged for a TGT
  2. TGT Storage: With recycle_tgt=True, the TGT is saved to .eptr2-tgt
  3. TGT Reuse: Subsequent calls reuse the stored TGT
  4. Auto Renewal: TGT is automatically renewed when expired
# Custom TGT storage location
eptr = EPTR2(
    use_dotenv=True,
    recycle_tgt=True,
    tgt_path="/path/to/store/tgt"
)

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use .env files - Keep credentials separate from code
  2. Enable TGT recycling - Reduces authentication overhead
  3. Add .env to .gitignore - Never commit credentials
  4. Use .env.example - Document required variables without values

Example .gitignore:

.env
.eptr2-tgt

Example .env.example:

EPTR_USERNAME=
EPTR_PASSWORD=

docs.title: "Username and password must be provided"
docs.text:
Ensure credentials are properly set:

import os
print("Username set:", "EPTR_USERNAME" in os.environ)
print("Password set:", "EPTR_PASSWORD" in os.environ)

    start_date,    # Start date in "YYYY-MM-DD" format
    end_date,      # End date in "YYYY-MM-DD" format

docs.title: Version 1.4.0 (2026-10-30)
docs.text: Endpoint mappings were reviewed against EPİAŞ's technical documentation (electricity, natural gas, reporting) and every call key was exercised against the live API.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Minimum versions raised to patched releases: urllib3>=2.8.0 (runtime dependency; chunked-response memory and HTTPS-proxy TLS advisories) and fastmcp>=3.4.10 in the mcp / allextras extras (component authorization advisory). The lock file also moves mcp 1.30.0, PyJWT 2.15.1, anyio 4.14.2 and opentelemetry-api 1.45.2 to their patched versions, staying on the same major versions.
  • The patched versions are also minimums in pyproject.toml (not only in the lock file), in the mcp / allextras extras: mcp>=1.30.0, pyjwt>=2.15.0, anyio>=4.14.2, opentelemetry-api>=1.45.1.
  • certifi>=2026.10.19 in the mcp / allextras / docs extras and the docs dependency group: earlier bundles trust emSign roots whose intermediate CA keys were compromised (GHSA-6q48-6c7w-9gw2, critical). certifi reaches eptr2 only through the MCP stack (httpx); eptr2's own API calls use the system trust store.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• calculate_kupst_cost_by_contract, calculate_diff_costs_by_contract and calculate_unit_price_and_costs_by_contract took KÜPST tolerance or multiplier from the regulation period's base table instead of the contract's date; include_maintenance_penalty overrode a multiplier passed in.
  • gather_and_calculate_plant_costs applied today's tolerance to every hour and the other multiplier to every plant type.
  • get_dabi_idm_data / get_day_ahead_and_bilateral_matches: documented columns and signs (nets are long minus short = net purchases), the per-organization GİP bid/ask swap (clearingQuantityAsk = bought, clearingQuantityBid = sold), and a new net_sales column (positive = net seller). get_dabi_idm_data_period and the GİP fetch now pass **kwargs (retry and timeout options were dropped). Offline regression test with a stubbed client.
  • capacity-demand and intl-capacity-demand-direction-list called the line-capacities endpoints (#6); they now return capacity-auction requests (auctionCode, requestedCapacity, allocatedCapacity, clearencePrice, …).
  • eligible-consumer-quantity requires start_date/end_date (it always returned HTTP 400).
  • ra-meters with ra_spg_name (and get_ra_meters) raised TypeError; the filter now maps to subscriberProfileGroupName.
  • ra-meter-volumes-period / -version: optional parameters were registered under a misspelled key and dropped; the profile-group filter is subscriber_pg.
  • Optional parameters passed as None are no longer sent (a None date crashed the generated wrappers).
  • page-update-date raised under the default postprocess=True.
  • Help entries for idm-order-history and ng-physical-realization.
  • calculate_unit_imbalance_price_by_contract and calculate_unit_imbalance_cost_by_contract used the price ceiling in force TODAY, not on the contract's date: January–March 2026 hours at the 3400 TL/MWh cap missed the 1.05 ceiling surcharge (483 of 15,635 published hours 2025-01..2026-10 differed from mcp-smp-imb; 0 after the fix). They now resolve floor and ceiling from the contract like the other *_by_contract helpers; explicit floor_price / ceil_price still win.
  • get_time_min_max_price_map: the 3,000 TL/MWh cap (GİP 3,090) starts on 2024-07-01, not 2024-06-01. In June 2024 PTF and SMF topped out at exactly 2,700 and GİP trades at exactly 2,781 (= 2,700 × 1.03); the first 3,000 / 3,090 prices are on 2024-07-01. June 2024 contracts now resolve to the 2,700 cap (contract_to_floor_ceil_prices, the *_by_contract imbalance helpers).
  • get_time_min_max_price_map: the GİP (IDM) ceiling is 3,760 TL/MWh from 2023-02-01 (was 3,759.5) and 3,142 from 2023-03-01 (was 3,141.5). EPİAŞ rounds 1.03 × the PTF cap up to the lira: February 2023 PH contracts traded at most 3,760.00 (121 trades at exactly that price, none above) and March 2023 at most 3,142.00 (142 trades, none above).
  • get_uevcb_ids (and the periodic_orgs wrappers that call it) capped the current month at the process's local date instead of today's date in Istanbul: on a host behind Turkey (e.g. Europe/Berlin, UTC) the last day queried was yesterday between Istanbul midnight and local midnight. It now uses Istanbul wall-clock time.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Main cost functions in eptr2.util.costs, working with or without pandas:
  • calculate_imbalance_prices(start_date, end_date, ...): hourly imbalance prices, unit costs and every parameter used (regulation period, floor/ceiling, V, B, margins, KÜPST tolerance, multiplier and floor), resolved per hour. MCP, SMP and system direction are fetched from mcp-smp-imb unless prices is given. EPİAŞ's published imbalance prices are used where available (imb_price_source); they are calculated only for hours without them (scenarios, offline use). Hours without SMP, such as the rest of the current day, are skipped with a warning. include_calculated=True adds the calculated prices for comparison.
  • calculate_imbalance_costs(data, category=..., ...): imbalance and KÜPST costs of actual vs forecast rows, using calculate_imbalance_prices; the category (any naming convention) and producer/consumer can be set per row.
  • Regulation values that change over time come from one dated table (get_time_regulation_params_map) and are applied by every *_by_contract helper; explicit arguments still win. From the first delivery hour of 2026-11-01: V is 100 (was 150), and KÜPST tolerance and multiplier depend on the KÜPST category: wind 15% / 0.05, solar 8% / 0.05, generation with storage (plant_w_battery) 5% / 0.10, other 5% / 0.05, transmission-connected unlicensed 20% / 0.02, distribution-connected unlicensed (per participant) 25% / 0.01, standalone storage (battery) 20% / 0.02. The 0.08 maintenance multiplier applies to wind and solar from 30, other sources from 25 monthly fault entries (is_kupst_maintenance_penalty_applicable). source/category accepts these categories; normalize_kupst_category maps other naming conventions (Turkish labels, RES/GES/HES, BESS, ...) to them, and unlicensed maps to unlicensed_from_transmission.
  • get_org_estimated_activity composite: a company's estimated hourly activity over a date range. Splits day-ahead (GÖP + İA) open / intraday close (dabi_idm_close), intraday day trade (min(idm_long, idm_short)), the day-ahead (GÖP + İA) net position dabi_net and the total net position dabi_idm_net (to be consumed or generated), from the organization's GÖP, İA and GİP matchings only. include_pnl=True adds a fictitious PnL of day-ahead open / intraday close trades (dabi_idm_pnl) from MCP and the published intraday WAP. include_tad=True adds volatility metrics, not PnL: the TAD (total absolute deviation, quantity-weighted mean |price − WAP|) of each contract from the market-wide trade log (idm_log_longer) and day_trade_tad = day_trade × TAD. The log is much slower. verbose=True logs each step with timings. export_to_csv=True writes the raw data (positions, MCP, WAP, trade log, per-contract WAP/TAD) and the result to export_dir as CSV; check_existing=True reads files of the same period instead of fetching them. end_date must be before today (Europe/Istanbul). Helpers calculate_idm_contract_stats and calculate_org_activity are pure.
  • idm_log_longer(verbose=True) logs the trade count and duration of each request.
  • ren-capacity-old — YEKDEM installed capacity up to the YEKDEM deadline.
  • ren-participant-year-list — years available for ren-participant-list.

docs.title: Breaking
docs.text:
• Regulation periods: contracts from 2026-11-01 are period 26_02 (get_regulation_period_by_contract), 26_01 covers 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-31, and current means the newest period. Each period label pins its own parameter row (get_regulation_params).
  • Contract-free 2026 functions take their defaults from the newest parameter row instead of literals: V, B, margins and floor/ceiling in calculate_unit_imbalance_price_2026 / _cost_2026, KÜPST multiplier and floor, KÜPST tolerance and the 5% DSG tolerance. Calls without a contract or period now use V=100 (the 2026-11-01 values); pass V=150, regulation_period="26_01" or a contract to reproduce earlier results. Pre-2026 functions keep their fixed values.
  • Removed calculate_imb_cost_pre_2026, calculate_diff_cost_pre_2026 and calculate_kupsm_list, deprecated since 1.3.3 for removal in 1.4.0. (calculate_kupst_cost_list stays while the deprecated calculate_diff_costs_list uses it.)
  • capacity-demand returns different columns (the real endpoint's).
  • interim-mcp / get_interim_mcp take start_date only; the endpoint ignored end_date and returned the start day.
  • eligible-consumer-count drops district_name, pg_name, province_id; the endpoint never applied them.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text: This guide covers the fundamental patterns for using eptr2.

docs.title: The EPTR2 Class
docs.text:
The EPTR2 class is your main interface to the EPIAS Transparency Platform:

from eptr2 import EPTR2

eptr = EPTR2(
    use_dotenv=True,      # Load credentials from .env
    recycle_tgt=True,     # Reuse authentication tickets
    dotenv_path=".env",   # Path to .env file
)

docs.title: The call Method
docs.text:
The primary method for fetching data:

result = eptr.call(
    key="mcp",                    # API endpoint name
    start_date="2024-07-29",      # Start date (YYYY-MM-DD)
    end_date="2024-07-29",        # End date (YYYY-MM-DD)
    postprocess=True,             # Return DataFrame (default)
    request_kwargs={"timeout": 10} # Optional request settings
)

docs.title: Call Aliases
docs.text:
Many endpoints have multiple names (aliases):

# These are equivalent
df1 = eptr.call("mcp", start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29")
df2 = eptr.call("ptf", start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29")

# SMP/SMF aliases
df3 = eptr.call("smp", start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29")
df4 = eptr.call("smf", start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29")

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use TGT recycling - Reduces authentication overhead: 

    eptr = EPTR2(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)

  2. Set appropriate timeouts - Avoid hanging requests: 

    df = eptr.call("mcp", ..., request_kwargs={"timeout": 10})

  3. Handle empty responses - Check DataFrame before processing: 

    df = eptr.call("mcp", ...)
if df.empty:
    print("No data returned")

  4. Reuse EPTR2 instance - Create once, use multiple times: 

    eptr = EPTR2(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)

# Multiple calls with same instance
mcp = eptr.call("mcp", ...)
smp = eptr.call("smp", ...)

docs.title: Example: Complete Analysis
docs.text:
Combine consumption and price data for cost analysis:

from eptr2 import EPTR2
from eptr2.composite import (
    get_hourly_consumption_and_forecast_data,
    get_hourly_price_and_cost_data
)
import pandas as pd

# Initialize
eptr = EPTR2(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)

# Get consumption data
consumption_df = get_hourly_consumption_and_forecast_data(
    start_date="2024-07-01",
    end_date="2024-07-31",
    eptr=eptr
)

# Get price data
price_df = get_hourly_price_and_cost_data(
    start_date="2024-07-01",
    end_date="2024-07-31",
    eptr=eptr
)

# Merge for analysis
analysis = pd.merge(
    consumption_df,
    price_df,
    on=['dt'],
    how='inner'
)

# Calculate total cost
analysis['total_cost'] = analysis['consumption'] * analysis['mcp']
print(f"Total cost: {analysis['total_cost'].sum():,.2f} TL")

idm_log = idm_log_longer(

quantity in the log is in lots (1 lot = 0.1 MWh).

docs.title: Organization Estimated Activity
docs.text:
Estimates a company's hourly trading activity from its own matched quantities only: GÖP, İA and GİP matchings by organization id (get_dabi_idm_data, about a second per week):

from eptr2.composite import get_org_estimated_activity

df = get_org_estimated_activity(
    start_date="2026-10-01",
    end_date="2026-10-07",
    org_id=104000,
    eptr=eptr,
    include_pnl=True,   # + MCP, published WAP and dabi_idm_pnl (fast)
    verbose=True,       # progress with timings on stderr
)

include_tad=True adds idm_tad and day_trade_tad, volatility metrics rather than PnL; it doesn't need include_pnl. TAD needs the market-wide intraday trade log (about 20k trades a day), fetched by idm_log_longer in multi-day chunks, so it is much slower: roughly 30–70 s for a week, depending on EPİAŞ. idm_log_days_interval sets the chunk length.

Column Meaning day_trade min(idm_long, idm_short), bought and sold back within the intraday market dabi_net da_net + bi_net: day-ahead (GÖP + İA) net position dabi_idm_net dabi_net + idm_net; positive must be consumed, negative generated (subtract bi_net for GÖP + GİP only) dabi_idm_close Day-ahead (GÖP + İA) position reversed in the intraday market: min(abs(dabi_net), abs(idm_net)) when they have opposite signs mcp, idm_wap With include_pnl=True: MCP and the published intraday WAP idm_tad With include_tad=True: TAD (total absolute deviation), the quantity-weighted mean of abs(price - WAP) over the contract's trades in the log dabi_idm_pnl dabi_idm_close * sign(dabi_net) * (idm_wap - mcp); bilateral quantities are valued at MCP too day_trade_tad With include_tad=True: day_trade * idm_tad (TL), the price room around WAP the day-trade volume was traded in; a volatility metric, not a PnL

The PnL is fictitious: the company's own trade prices are not public. To analyse several companies with TAD, fetch the log once with idm_log_longer and pass it as idm_log_df, or use the CSV export:

for org_id in [104000, 105000]:
    df = get_org_estimated_activity(
        start_date="2026-10-01",
        end_date="2026-10-07",
        org_id=org_id,
        eptr=eptr,
        include_pnl=True,
        include_tad=True,
        export_to_csv=True,   # write raw data and result to export_dir
        check_existing=True,  # read files of the same period instead of fetching
        export_dir="data",
    )

export_to_csv=True writes {name}_{start_date}_{end_date}.csv files: org_{org_id}_positions, mcp, wap, idm_log, idm_contract_stats (WAP, TAD, trade count and volume per contract) and org_{org_id}_activity, for the steps that ran. With check_existing=True files of the same name are read instead of fetched, so the second organization above reuses the market-wide MCP, WAP and trade log. The files are CSV because the trade log can exceed Excel's row limit.

end_date must be before today (Europe/Istanbul); the function raises ValueError otherwise, because data of the current day isn't final.

docs.title: Convenience Wrappers (eptr2.calls)
docs.text:
Starting with v1.3.8, every endpoint exposed by EPTR2.call is also available as a typed top-level function under eptr2.calls. These are thin convenience wrappers around eptr.call(...) that give you:

  • Auto-complete in editors thanks to explicit parameter signatures.
  • Type hints for every parameter (str, str | int, list, bool).
  • Bilingual docstrings (EN/TR) with the endpoint category and a reference URL to the EPIAS Transparency documentation.
  • Optional eptr argument — pass your own EPTR2 instance or let the wrapper construct one lazily.

There is one get_* function per endpoint key, with hyphens replaced by underscores. Aliases (ptf, smf) get their own functions that route to the alias key.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from eptr2 import EPTR2
from eptr2.calls import get_mcp, get_smp, get_rt_cons

eptr = EPTR2(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)

mcp = get_mcp(start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29", eptr=eptr)
smp = get_smp(start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29", eptr=eptr)
cons = get_rt_cons(start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29", eptr=eptr)

docs.title: Lazy EPTR2 Construction
docs.text:
If eptr is omitted, the wrapper constructs EPTR2() on demand. This honours use_dotenv=True by default, so any .env credentials are picked up automatically:

from eptr2.calls import get_ptf

# No explicit client — wrapper builds EPTR2() internally
df = get_ptf(start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29")

For repeated calls, pass an instance so TGT recycling and any custom settings are preserved:

eptr = EPTR2(use_dotenv=True, recycle_tgt=True)
df1 = get_mcp(start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29", eptr=eptr)
df2 = get_smp(start_date="2024-07-29", end_date="2024-07-29", eptr=eptr)

docs.title: Function Signature
docs.text:
Each wrapper follows this shape:

def get_<endpoint>(
    <required_param>: <type>,
    ...
    <optional_param>: <type> | None = None,
    ...
    eptr: EPTR2 | None = None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """<EN title> / <TR title>
    ...
    """

Extra keyword arguments (e.g. postprocess=False) are forwarded straight to eptr.call.

docs.title: Forwarding Aliases
docs.text:
Aliases each get a dedicated function that routes to the alias key, so existing server-side resolution is honoured:

from eptr2.calls import get_mcp, get_ptf, get_smp, get_smf

# All four are real functions; each forwards its own key to eptr.call.

docs.title: Discovering Wrappers
docs.text:
import eptr2.calls as calls

# Every public name is included in __all__
print(len(calls.__all__))  # 236 (234 endpoints + 2 aliases)

# Get help for any wrapper
help(calls.get_mcp)

from eptr2.calls import get_dam_clearing

# org_id is optional and will be sent as null when omitted
df = get_dam_clearing(
    start_date="2024-07-01",

    org_id=123,

docs.title: When to Use eptr.call vs get_*
docs.text:
Use case Recommended Quick scripts / one-off calls get_* IDE auto-complete on parameter names get_* Reading bilingual docs in your editor get_* Dynamic endpoint selection (by string) eptr.call Iterating over all endpoint keys eptr.call

Both APIs use the same underlying request path — pick whichever fits the call site best.
